title: Chapter 4: Returning to the City
paragraphs: "What should I say when I call the police? That I was brought here by a turtle shell? That I've been kidnapped? Or just that I'm lost?"
Just as Chen Mobai nervously dialed the Immortal Sect Enforcement Division, something shocking happened. At this point, I urge readers to remember our domain: sto55.com.
His phone had no signal!
The call wouldn't go through!
On Diyuan Star, even at the bottom of the deep sea thousands of meters below, the Immortal Sect's Celestial Star network covered everything.

Chen Mobai even recalled hearing a Fifth-Tier Array Master proudly declare on television that even during the world-opening wars two millennia ago, Immortal Sect cultivators who had plunged into The Abyss could still access Diyuan Star's signal, ensuring seamless communication for every cultivator.
Where am I, exactly?
Chen Mobai's face was a mask of bewilderment.
He exhausted his entire mental library of knowledge, even thoroughly searching every safe area of the Water Abode, tapping every single paved brick on the ground.
But in the end, Chen Mobai could only sit down helplessly on the floor of the Front Hall.
He couldn't find a single clue about how to escape.
Just as he was about to resign himself to fate and meditate, a silver glow suddenly lit up his phone screen, drawing his attention.
He noticed a software icon had suddenly appeared on his phone—one he had never downloaded before.
The icon was a small, dark green turtle.
Below it, the software name read:
Turtle Gem!
What's this?
Chen Mobai instinctively moved his finger to the icon, intending to uninstall it. He refused to allow software on his phone that he didn't recognize.
But then, a red message flashed on the screen:Cannot Uninstall.
What the—?!
This phone is completely out of control!
Chen Mobai was about to angrily shut down and restart the device when a sudden realization struck him.
Turtle Gem... could it be... the Turtle Shell?!
He hurriedly tapped the icon, opening the software.
The action went smoothly, without any glitches.
The main interface was simple, featuring only three function buttons:Teleport,Recall, andProxy.

Chen Mobai was both thrilled and apprehensive. He closed and reopened the Turtle Gem app to confirm there were no instructions, then tentatively tapped theRecallbutton with a slightly trembling finger, relying on his own interpretation of its function.
This process requires an eight-second guiding period. During this time, no interference is allowed. Host, please find a quiet location.
The moment he tapped the Recall button, this message suddenly appeared on his phone screen.

Even as Chen Mobai pondered what constituted "disturbing" the process, a silver light suddenly flashed, enveloping him completely. It swirled around him like a vortex, tearing open a rift in the void, and whisked him away from the Water Abode.
Already back?
When the silver light faded, Chen Mobai found himself standing in his room again, his hand still resting on the Turtle Shell.

He yanked his hand back with lightning speed, retreated to his bed, and grabbed the Demon-Subduing Sword hanging on the wall—a child's replica his father had bought him at the Grotto-Heaven Scenic Area when he was a boy.
The sword gleamed brightly, but its miniature size—only thirty centimeters long—made it clear it was purely ornamental.
For about two minutes, the room remained eerily silent.
Chen Mobai stared at the Turtle Shell, pondering what to do with it, when the sound of the front door opening drifted up from downstairs.
It was his mother returning home.
The familiar sounds of the door opening and closing confirmed her arrival.
Since Chen Mobai had hung a "Cultivating—Do Not Disturb" sign on his door, his mother didn't come up to bother him, but he could still hear her familiar grumbling.
"That boy... I keep telling him to cultivate at the Spiritual Vein's meditation chamber, but he still prefers to hole up in his room..."
Chen Mobai hesitated, then decided against going downstairs.
He gently sheathed the child's Demon-Subduing Sword and used the Lightness Technique to float down to the Turtle Shell, examining it closely.

The next morning, Chen Mobai descended the stairs, his spirits low. After enduring his mother's nagging, he ate a carefully prepared breakfast, slung his backpack over his shoulder, and rushed to catch the bus.
After morning self-study, an old man dressed in simple, unadorned clothing entered the classroom punctually.
"Good morning, Teacher Ding!" the students chorused, rising to their feet.
Old Man Ding nodded calmly. "Today, we will continue our lecture on the solidification of defensive spell formations..."
The Immortal Sect's curriculum divides the subjects all cultivators must study into four main disciplines:
Techniques, Alchemy, Artifact Forging, and Formations.

These four disciplines are further subdivided into dozens of specialized courses. By their final year of high school, students must choose one as their primary focus, laying the foundation for their future studies.
This is analogous to the division between arts and sciences in high schools on Diyuan Star before the advent of immortal cultivation civilization.
However, now there are four disciplines to choose from in cultivation.

After all, to gain admission to a Great Dao Academy, one must not only excel in the national college entrance examination and demonstrate a certain level of cultivation but also, crucially, pass the academy's own rigorous assessment.
Chen Mobai and his classmates had all chosen[Technique Studies]as their primary discipline.
Chen Mobai didn't know why others chose Technique Studies. For him, it was simply the most economical option.
The other disciplines—Alchemy Studies, Artifact Forging Studies, and even Formation Studies—all required significant resources and Merit Points for practice and advancement.
Technique Studies, on the other hand, was straightforward:
Moreover, Technique Studies offered the path to becoming a Talisman Master, a profession with exceptionally promising earning potential among the myriad cultivation arts.
Chen Mobai had aspired to become a Talisman Art Master since childhood.

He had a family foundation; his mother worked at a Talisman Paper manufacturing factory, and through exposure to the craft, he had gained some insight. This would allow him to get a head start, freeing up more time for cultivation.
Old Man Ding, whose full name was Ding Jinglue, was a well-respected cultivator in Danxia City.
In his youth, Ding Jinglue possessed decent talent—a three-attribute True Spiritual Root, slightly superior to Chen Mobai's.

His performance on the college entrance exam was mediocre, barely securing him admission to the local Dan Zhu Academy. Yet, driven by unwavering determination, he studied diligently for twenty years at Dan Zhu Academy. Eventually, he passed the Immortal Ascension Assessment of the Ten Great Palaces, earning exceptional admission.
But his breakthrough came too late.

Even after entering the Pure Yang Palace, reaching Qi Refinement Completion before the age of sixty (his life's limit), and obtaining the Foundation Establishment Secret Art, he still failed to achieve his goal.

Having exhausted his one chance at Foundation Establishment in the Pure Yang Palace, Ding Jinglue endured another twenty years of arduous cultivation, returning once more to Qi Refinement Completion. With unwavering determination, he attempted to break through to Foundation Establishment again.
Alas, fortune did not favor him, and Ding Jinglue failed once more.
After these two failed attempts, having exhausted all his potential, Ding Jinglue returned to his birthplace, Danxia City, and became a teacher.

Before attempting Foundation Establishment, he had devoted himself entirely to cultivation. But after returning home, he found himself with ample time to delve into the myriad arts of immortal cultivation.
Among these, he excelled in spellcasting, a path requiring no capital investment. However, his teaching skills were mediocre, often lulling most students into a drowsy stupor.
Normally, Chen Mobai would also slack off in class. But today was different.
